review_notes: I read the whole 54-line file. `planarVolume_absolutelyContinuous_sphericalArea`, `scalar_unit_spherical`, `scalar_unit` and `scalar_aestronglyMeasurable` are thin wrappers around existing API, so I did not flag them. I grepped `MemLp.of_bound` under the CircleDomains directory. The only repeated pattern I found was "a function with values in [0,1] is in L^p on a finite measure". It appears in `scalar_memLp_on`, `filled_memLp` (Transfer/BoundedScalarFillings.lean), `locallyIntegrable_of_unit_bound` (Topology/BoundedCompactCutoff.lean) and `ae_mem_unitInterval_of_weak_limit` (Sobolev/BoundedWeakRange.lean). Each copy is only a few lines, so this is a modest finding. I did not check the import graph, so the home file for the helper is a suggestion. I did not look for a Mathlib lemma that already states this exactly, and did not compile anything.

findings.excerpt:
apply MemLp.of_bound W.scalar_aestronglyMeasurable.restrict 1
  filter_upwards [ae_restrict_of_ae W.scalar_unit] with z hz
  rw [Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_of_nonneg hz.1]
  exact hz.2
findings.problem: The step "a function that is a.e. in [0,1] has norm ≤ 1, hence is MemLp on a finite measure" is written out by hand in at least four proofs. The same four-line block (`MemLp.of_bound … 1`, then `Real.norm_eq_abs`, `abs_of_nonneg`, `.2`) appears here, in `filled_memLp`, in `locallyIntegrable_of_unit_bound`, and in the `hi` step of `ae_mem_unitInterval_of_weak_limit`. Each copy re-proves the same bound, so a change to the convention (for example the exponent or the finite-measure handling) has to be made in every copy.
findings.proposed_change:
Add one helper in a base file imported by all four users, for example next to `ae_mem_unitInterval_of_weak_limit` in Sobolev/BoundedWeakRange.lean:

theorem memLp_of_ae_mem_unitInterval {α : Type*} [MeasurableSpace α] {μ : Measure α} [IsFiniteMeasure μ] {f : α → ℝ} {p : ℝ≥0∞} (hm : AEStronglyMeasurable f μ) (hf : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, f x ∈ Icc (0:ℝ) 1) : MemLp f p μ := MemLp.of_bound hm 1 (hf.mono fun x hx => by rw [Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_of_nonneg hx.1]; exact hx.2)

Then `scalar_memLp_on` becomes:
  let : IsFiniteMeasure ((volume : Measure ℂ).restrict K) := isFiniteMeasure_restrict.mpr hK
  exact memLp_of_ae_mem_unitInterval W.scalar_aestronglyMeasurable.restrict (ae_restrict_of_ae W.scalar_unit)

`filled_memLp` becomes `memLp_of_ae_mem_unitInterval F.filled_measurable.aestronglyMeasurable (Eventually.of_forall F.filled_mem)`.
`locallyIntegrable_of_unit_bound` uses `(memLp_of_ae_mem_unitInterval (p := 2) hm.restrict (Eventually.of_forall hf)).integrable (by norm_num)`.
The `hi n` step in `ae_mem_unitInterval_of_weak_limit` uses the same lemma with `Eventually.of_forall (hb n)`.
findings.benefit: The unit-interval-to-L^p reasoning is proved once and each use is a one-line application. The four proofs get shorter, and readers see directly that only the measurability and the a.e. [0,1] range are used. Later users such as scalar limits or fillings can reuse the lemma instead of copying the block again.

evidence.excerpt:
apply MemLp.of_bound F.filled_measurable.aestronglyMeasurable 1
  exact Eventually.of_forall fun z => by
    rw [Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_of_nonneg (F.filled_mem z).1]
    exact (F.filled_mem z).2

apply MemLp.of_bound (hm n) 1
    exact Eventually.of_forall fun x => by
      rw [Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_of_nonneg (hb n x).1]
      exact (hb n x).2
